newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning seeks potential breast implant claims.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning seeks potential breast implant claims.

text.p: Dow Corning Corp, a joint venture of Dow Chemical Co and Corning Inc, on Thursday said the bankruptcy court-ordered U.S. deadline for filing a claim against it because of the use of its breast and other implants was next January 15.

Dow Corning, which had no estimate how many people might file claims, said that potential U.S. claimants who did not file by that deadline might forever be barred from making a claim. It did, however, grant a 30-day extension to claimants outside U.S., to February 14.
To qualify for it, a claimant would have to continuously maintain residence outside the U.S., its territories and Puerto Rico during the period September 15, 1996 through November 15, 1996.
Thousands of women fitted with the silicon implants have claimed to have become ill with connective tissue diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis.

Dow Corning and other implant makers had been named defendants in a class action law suit, but when a settlement was reached, many of the recipients of the implants dropped out and filed individual cases against Dow.
Facing possibly thousands of individual trials, Dow Corning filed for bankruptcy last May 15.

Dow Corning said at a news conference that the effort to seek possible claimants was a step in the court's effort to resolve claims against the company. Company spokeswoman Barie Carmichael said that "whether the claim will be disputed, allowed or disallowed will be determined at a later date."

She said Dow Corning would try to reach potential claimants through television and print advertising in the United States and foreign countries where its products were sold from the early 1960s until taken off the market in 1992.
In addition to breast implants, the company was also seeking to reach claimants with other types of implants.
